items.remediation: Use explicit deny defaults, transactional auth state, strict exception handling, dependency timeouts, and tests for failure branches.
items.safety: Do not induce production dependency outages; use malformed local inputs or owner-provided fault-injection evidence.

items.title: Require recent step-up authentication for sensitive operations
items.objective: Determine whether high-risk account, financial, administrative, or data-export actions rely only on an old session.
prerequisites: A designated disposable test account
An approved authentication flow and safe stopping point
steps: Identify owner-defined sensitive actions and safe stopping points
Use a deliberately aged test session where feasible
Attempt the action without recent factor proof
Complete approved step-up and compare assurance/session changes

references.title: Authentication vulnerabilities

items.remediation: Define action assurance/freshness policy, require transaction-bound step-up, and rotate or annotate session assurance after verification.
items.safety: Use reversible test actions and stop before payments, deletion, privilege grant, or irreversible export unless explicitly approved.

references.title: Authentication vulnerabilities

items.remediation: Notify through pre-existing channels, include event context and recovery path, avoid secrets, and log/alert security events centrally.
items.safety: Use controlled inboxes/numbers and one event per channel to avoid message abuse.

An approved authentication flow and safe stopping point
steps: Review owner-approved event schemas or sanitized test logs
Generate one success and one failure with synthetic values
Correlate account alias, result, factor type, source context, and request ID
Verify passwords, OTPs, reset tokens, assertions, and full session tokens are absent

items.remediation: Generate server-side single-use challenges, bind user/RP/origin, verify all WebAuthn results, require recent auth, and notify the account owner.

references.title: Web Authentication: Level 3

items.remediation: Use short-lived single-use challenges, validate clientDataJSON and authenticatorData fully, enforce UV policy, and monitor cloned-credential signals.
